verses.t: Love righteousness, you that be judges of the earth: think of the Lord with a good (heart) and in simplicity of heart seeke him.
For he will be found of them that tempt him not: and shews himself to such as do not distrust him.
For froward thoughts separate from God: and his power when it is tryed, reproous the vnwise.
For into a malitious soul wisdom shall not enter: nor dwell in the body that is subiect to sin.
For the holy spirit of discipline will flie deceit, & remoue from thoughts that are without vnderstanding: and will not abide when vnrighteousnesse comes in.
For wisdom is a louing spirit: and will not acquite a blasphemour of his words: for God is witness of his reines, and a true beholder of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.
For the spirit of the Lord fills the world: and that which contains all things has knowledge of the voice.
Therefore he that speaks unrighteous things, cannot be hid: neither shal vengeance, when it punishes. passe by him.
For inquisition shall be made into the counsels of the vngodly: and the sound of his words, shall come to the Lord, for the manifestation of his wicked deeds.
For the eare of iealousie hears al things: and the noise of murmurings is not hid.
Therefore beware of murmuring, which is vnprofitable, and refraine your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belies, slays the soul.
Seeke not death in the errour of your life: and pull not upon yourselves destruction, with the works of your hands.
For God made not death: neither has he pleasure in the destruction of the living.
For he created all things, that they might have their being: and the generations of the world were healthfull: and there is no poyson of destruction in them: nor the kingdom of death upon the earth.
For righteousness is immortall.

But vngodly men with their works, and words called it to them: for when they thought to have it their friend, they consumed to nought, and made a couenant with it, because they are worthy to take part with it.

verses.t: For the vngodly said, reasoning with themselues, but not aright: Our life is short and tedious, and in the death of a man there is no remedie: neither was there any man knowen to have returned from the graue.
For we are borne at all aduenture: & we shall be heereafter as though we had never bene: for the breath in our nostrils is as smoke, and a litle sparke in the mouing of our heart.
Which being extinguished, our body shall be turned into ashes, and our spirit shall vanish as the soft aire:

And our name shall be forgotten in time, and no man shall have our works in remembrance, and our life shall passe away as the trace of a cloud: and shall be dispersed as a mist that is driuen away with the beames of the Sun, and ouercome with the heat of it.
For our time is a very shadow that passes away: and after our end there is no returning: for it is fast sealed, so that no man comes again.
Come on therefore, let us enioy the good things that are present: and let us speedily vse the creatures like as in youth.
Let us fill our selves with costly wine, and ointments: and let no flower of the Spring passe by us.
Let us crowne our selves with Rose buds, before they be withered.
Let none of us go without his part of our voluptuousnesse: let us leaue tokens of our ioyfulnesse in every place: for this is our portion, and our lot is this.
Let us oppresse the poore righteous man, let us not spare the widow, nor reuerence the ancient gray haires of the aged.
Let our strength be the Lawe of justice: for that which is feeble is found to be nothing worth.

Therefore let us lye in wait for the righteous: because he is not for our turne, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he vpbraids us with our offending the Law, and obiects to our infamy the transgressings of our education.
He profess to have the knowledge of God: and he calls himself the childe of the Lord.
He was made to reprooue our thoughts.
He is grieuous to us euen to beholde: for his life is not like other mens, his waies are of another fashion.
We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstains from our wayes as from filthinesse: he pronouncs the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that God is his father.
Let us see if his words be true: and let us proue what shall happen in the end of him.
For if the just man be the son of God, he will helpe him, and deliuer him from the hand of his enemies.
Let us examine him with despitefulnesse and torrture, that we may know his meekenesse, and prooue his patience.
Let us condemne him with a shamefull death: for by his own saying, he shall be respected.
Such things they did imagine, and were deceiued: for their own wickedness has blinded them.
As for the mysteries of God, they knew them not: neither hoped they for the wages of righteousness: nor discerned a reward for blamelesse souls.
For God created man to be immortall, and made him to be an image of his own eternitie.
Neuerthelesse through enuie of the devil came death into the world: and they that do holde of his side do find it.

verses.t: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.
In the sight of the vnwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery,
And their going from us to be vtter destruction: but they are in peace.
For though they be punished in the sight of men: yet is their hope full of immortalitie.
And hauing bene a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for God proued them, and found them worthy for himself.
As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and receiued them as a burnt offering.
And in the time of their visitation, they shall shine and runne to and fro, like sparkes among the stubble.
They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Lord shall raigne for ever.
They that put their trust in him, shall vnderstand the truth: and such as be faithfull in love, shall abide with him: for grace & mercy is to his saints, and he has care for his elect.
But the vngodly shall be punished according to their own imaginations, which have neglected the righteous, and forsaken the Lord.
For who so despises wisdom, and nurture, he is miserable, and their hope is vaine, their labours vnfruitfull, and their works vnprofitable.
Their wiues are foolish, and their children wicked.
Their of-spring is cursed: therefore blessed is the barren that is vndefiled, which has not knowen the sinfull bed: she shall have fruit in the visitation of souls.

And blessed is the Eunuch which with his hands has wrought no iniquitie: nor imagined wicked things against God: for to him shall be given the speciall gift of faith, and an inheritance in the Temple of the Lord more acceptable to his minde.
For glorious is the fruit of good labours: and the root of wisedom shall never fall away.
As for the children of adulterers, they shall not come to their perfection, and the seed of an unrighteous bed shal be rooted out.
For though they live long, yet shall they be nothing regarded: and their last age shall be without honor.
Or if they die quickly, they have no hope, neither comfort in the day of triall.
For horrible is the end of the unrighteous generation.

verses.t: Better it is to have no children, and to have virtue: for the memoriall of it is immortal: because it is knowen with God and with men.
When it is present, men take example at it, and when it is gone they desire it: it wears a crown, and triumphs for ever, hauing gotten the victory, striuing for vndefiled rewards.
But the multiplying brood of the vngodly shall not thriue, nor take deepe rooting from bastard slips, nor lay any fast foundation.
For though they flourish in branches for a time: yet standing not fast, they shall be shaken with the winde: and through the force of windes they shall be rooted out.
The vnperfect branches shall be broken off, their fruit vnprofitable, not ripe to eat: indeed meet for nothing.
For children begotten of vnlawfull beds, are witnesses of wickednes against their parents in their triall.
But though the righteous be preuented with death: yet shal he be in rest.
For honourable age is not that which stands in length of time, nor that is measured by number of years.
But wisdom is the gray haire to men, & an vnspotted life is old age.
He pleased God, and was beloued of him: so that living among sinners, he was translated.
Indeed, speedily was he taken away, lest that wickednes should alter his vnderstanding, or deceit beguile his soul.
For the bewitching of naughtines does obscure things that are honest: and the wandring of concupiscence, does vndermine the simple mind.
He being made perfect in a short time, fulfilled a long time.
For his soul pleased the Lord: therefore hasted he to take him away, from among the wicked.
This the people saw, and vnderstood it not: neither laid they up this in their mindes, That his grace and mercy is with his Saints, and that he has respect to his chosen.
Thus the righteous that is dead, shall condemne the vngodly, which are living, and youth that is soone perfected, the many years and old age of the unrighteous.
For they shall see the end of the wise, & shall not vnderstand what God in his counsell has decreed of him, and to what end the Lord has set him in safetie.
They shal see him and despise him, but God shall laugh them to scorne, and they shal hereafter be a vile carkeis, and a reproch among the dead for euermore.

For he shall rend them, and cast them downe headlong, that they shall be speechles: and he shal shake them from the foundation: and they shall be vtterly laid waste, and be in sorow: and their memoriall shall perish.
And when they cast up the accounts of their sins, they shall come with feare: and their own iniquities shall conuince them to their face.

verses.t: Then shal the righteous man stand in great boldnesse, before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.
When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible feare, & shall be amazed at the strangenesse of his saluation, so farre beyond all that they looked for.
And they repenting, and groning for anguish of spirit, shall say within themselues, This was he whom we had sometimes in derision, and a prouerbe of reproch.
We fooles accounted his life madnes, and his end to be without honor.
How is he numbred among the children of God, and his lot is among the Saints?
Therefore have we erred from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness has not shined to us, and the Sun of righteousness rose not upon us.
We wearied ourselues in the way of wickedness, and destruction: indeed, we have gone through deserts, where there lay no way: but as for the way of the Lord, we have not knowen it.
What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?
All those things are passed away like a shadow, and as a Poste that hasted by.
And as a ship that passes over the waues of the water, which when it is gone by, the trace of it cannot be found: neither the path way of the keele in the waues.

Or as when a bird has flowen thorow the aire, there is no token of her way to be found, but the light aire being beaten with the stroke of her wings, and parted with the violent noise and motion of them, is passed thorow, and therin afterwards no signe where she went, is to be found.
Or like as when an arrow is shot at a marke, it parts the aire, which immediatly comes together again: so that a man cannot know where it went thorow:
Euen so we in like maner, assoone as we were borne, began to draw to our end, and had no signe of virtue to show: but were consumed in our own wickedness.

For the hope of the vngodly is like dust that is blowen away with þ wind, like a thinne froth that is driuen away with þ storme: like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passes away as the remembrance of a guest that taries but a day.
But þ righteous live for euermore, their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High.
Therfore shall they receiue a glorious kingdom, & a beautiful crowne from the Lords hande: for with his right hand shall he couer them, and with his arme shall he protect them.
He shall take to him his ielousie for cōplete armour, & make the creature his weapon for the reuenge of his enemies.
He shal put on righteousness as a brestplate, and true judgment in stead of an helmet.
He shall take holinesse for an inuincible shield.
His seuere wrath shall he sharpen for a sword, and the world shall fight with him against the vnwise.
Then shal the right-aiming thunder bolts go abroad, and from the cloudes, as from a well-drawen bow, shall they flie to the marke.
And hailestones full of wrath shal be cast as out of a stonebow, and the water of the Sea shall rage against them, & the floods shall cruelly drowne them.
Indeed a mightie wind shall stand up against them, & like a storme shall blow them away: thus iniquity shal lay were the whole earth, and ill dealing shall ouerthrow the thrones of the mightie.

verses.t: Heare therefore, O you kings, and vnderstand, learne you that be judges of the ends of the earth.
Give eare you that rule the people, and glory in the multitude of nations.
For power is given you of the Lord, & soueraigntie from the Highest, who shall try your works; and search out your counsels.
Because being Ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after the counsell of God,
Horribly and speedily shall he come upon you: for a sharpe judgment shall be to them that be in high places.
For mercy will soone pardon the mean: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.
For he which is Lord over all, shall feare no mans person: neither shall he stand in awe of any mans greatnesse: for he has made the small and great, and cares for all alike.
But a sore triall shall come upon the mighty.
To you therefore, O kings, do I speake, that you may learne wisdom, and not fall away.
For they that keepe holinesse holily, shall be judged holy: and they that have learned such things, shall find what to answere.
Therefore set your affection upon my words, desire them, and you shall be instructed.
Wisdom is glorious and never fades away: indeed she is easily seene of them that love her, and found of such as seeke her.
She preuents them that desire her, in making herself first knowen to them.
Whoever seeks her earely, shall have no great trauaile: for he shall find her sitting at his doores.
To think therefore upon her is perfection of wisdom: and who so watches for her, shall quickly be without care.
For she goes about seeking such as are worthy of her, shews herself fauourably to them in the wayes, and meets them in every thought.
For the very true beginning of her, is the desire of discipline, and the care of discipline is love:
And love is the keeping of her lawes; and the giuing heed to her lawes, is the assurance of incorruption.
And incorruption makes us near to God.
Therefore the desire of wisdom brings to a kingdom.
If your delight be then in thrones and scepters, O you kings of the people, honor wisdom that you may raigne for euermore.

As for wisdom what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you: but will seeke her out from the beginning of her natiuity, & bring the knowledge of her into light, and will not passe over the truth.
Neither will I go with consuming enuy: for such a man shall have no fellowship with wisdom.
But the multitude of the wise is the welfare of the world: and a wise king is the vpholding of the people.
Receiue therefore instruction thorough my words, and it shall do you good.

As for wisdom what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you: but will seeke her out from the beginning of her natiuity, & bring the knowledge of her into light, and will not passe over the truth. Neither will I go with consuming enuy: for such a man shall have no fellowship with wisdom.
But the multitude of the wise is the welfare of the world: and a wise king is the vpholding of the people. Receiue therefore instruction thorough my words, and it shall do you good.

verses.t: I myself also am a mortall man, like to all, and the ofspring of him that was first made of the earth,
And in my mothers wombe was fashioned to be flesh in the time of tenne moneths being compacted in blood, of the seed of man, and the pleasure that came with sleepe.
And when I was borne, I drew in the common aire, and fell upon the earth which is of like nature, and the first voice which I vttered, was crying as all others do.
I was nursed in swadling clothes, and that with cares.
For there is no king that had any other beginning of birth.
For all men have one entrance to life, and the like going out.
Therefore I prayed, and vnderstanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.
I preferred her before scepters, and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.
Neither compared I to her any precious stone, because all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and siluer shall be counted as clay before her.
I loved her aboue health and beautie, and chose to have her in stead of light: for the light that comes from her never goes out.
All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands.
And I reioyced in them all, because wisdom goes before them: and I knew not that she was the mother of them.
I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.
For she is a treasure to men that never fails: which they that vse, become the friends of God: being commended for the gifts that come from learning.
God has granted me to speake as I would, and to conceiue as is meet for the things that are given me: because it is he that leads to wisdom, and directs the wise.
For in his hand are both we and our words: all wisdom also and knowledge of workemanship.
For he has given me certaine knowledge of the things that are, namely to know how the world was made, & the operation of the elements:
The beginning, ending, and midst of the times: the alterations of the turning of the Sun, and the change of seasons:
The circuits of yeres, and the positions of starres:
The natures of living creatures, and the furies of wilde beasts: the violence of windes, and the reasonings of men: the diuersities of plants, and the vertues of rootes:
And all such things as are either secret or manifest: them I know.

For wisdom which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an vnderstanding spirit holy, one onely, manifold, subtile, liuely, cleare, vndefiled, plaine, not subiect to hurt, louing the thing that is good, quicke, which cānot be letted, ready to do good:
Kinde to man, stedfast, sure, free from care, hauing all power, ouerseeing all things, and going through all vnderstanding, pure, and most subtile spirits.
For wisdom is more moouing then any motion: she passes and goes through all things by reason of her purenesse.
For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no vndefiled thing fall into her.
For she is the brightnesse of the euerlasting light: the vnspotted mirrour of the power of God, and the Image of his goodnesse.
And being but one she can do all things: and remayning in her self, she makes all things new: and in all ages entring into holy souls, she makes them friends of God, & Prophets.
For God loves none but him, that dwells with wisdom.
For she is more beautiful then the Sun, and aboue all the order of starres, being compared with the light, she is found before it.
For after this comes night: but vice shall not preuaile against wisdome.

verses.t: Wisdome reaches from one ende to another mightily: and sweetly does she order all things.
I loved her and sought her out, from my youth I dedesired to make her my spouse, and I was a louer of her beautie.
In that she is conuersant with God, she magnifies her nobilitie: indeed, the Lord of all things himself loved her.
For she is priuy to the mysteries of the knowledge of God, and a louer of his works.
If riches be a possession to be desired in this life: what is richer then wisdom that works all things?
And if prudence work; who of all that are, is a more cunning workeman then she?
And if a man love righteousness, her labours are vertues: for she teaches temperance and prudence: justice and fortitude, which are such things as men can have nothing more profitable in their life.

If a man desire much experience: she knows things of old, and coniecturs aright what is to come: she knows the subtilties of speaches, and can expound darke sentences: she foreses signes and wonders, and the euents of seasons and times.
Therefore I purposed to take her to me to live with me, knowing that she would be a counsellour of good things, and a comfort in cares & griefe.
For her sake I shall have estimation among the multitude, and honor with the Elders, though I be yong.
I shall be found of a quicke conceit in judgment, and shall be admired in the sight of great men.
When I hold my tongue they shal bide my leisure, and when I speake they shall give good eare to me: if I talke much, they shall lay their handes upon their mouth.
Moreouer, by the meanes of her, I shall obtaine immortalitie, and leaue behind me an euerlasting memoriall to them that come after me.
I shall set the people in order, and the nations shall be subiect to me.
Horrible tyrants shall be afraide when they do but heare of me, I shall be found good among the multitude, and valiant in warre.
After I am come into mine house, I will repose myself with her: for her conuersation has no bitternes, and to live with her, has no sorrow, but mirth and ioy.

verses.t: O God of my fathers, and Lord of mercy, who have made all things with your word,
And ordained man through your wisdom, that he should have dominion over the creatures, which you have made,
And order the world according to equitie and righteousness, and execute judgment with an vpright heart:
Give me wisdom that sits by your Throne, and reiect me not from among your children:
For I your seruant and son of your handmaide, am a feeble person, and of a short time, and too young for the vnderstanding of judgment and lawes.
For though a man be never so perfect among the children of men, yet if your wisdom be not with him, he shall be nothing regarded.
You have chosen me to be a king of your people, and a Judge of your sons and daughters:
You have commaunded me to build a Temple upon your holy mount, and an Altar in the city wherein you dwell, a resemblance of the holy Tabernacle which you have prepared from the beginning:
And wisdom was with you: which knows your works, and was present when you made the world, and knew what was acceptable in your sight, and right in your Commaundements.
O send her out of your holy heauens, and from the Throne of your glory, that being present she may labour with me, that I may know what is pleasing to you.
For she knows and vnderstands all things, and she shall leade me soberly in my doings, and preserue me in her power.
So shall my works be acceptable, and then shall I judge your people righteously, and be worthy to sit in my fathers seate.
For what man is he that can know the counsell of God? or who can think what the will of the Lord is?
For the thoughts of mortall men are miserable, and our deuices are but vncertaine.
For the corruptible body press downe the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weighs downe the minde that muses upon many things.
And hardly do we gesse aright at things that are upon earth, and with labour do we find the things that are before us: but the things that are in heaven, who has searched out?
And your counsell who has knowen, except you give wisdom, and send your holy spirit from aboue?
For so the wayes of them which lived on the earth were reformed, and men were taught the things that are pleasing to you, and were saved through wisdom.

verses.t: She preserued the first formed father of the world that was created alone, and brought him out of his fall,
And gaue him power to rule all things.
But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherwith he murdered his brother.
For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood, Wisdom again preserued it, & directed the course of the righteous, in a piece of wood, of small value.

Moreouer, the nations in their wicked conspiracie being confounded, she found out the righteous, and preserued him blamelesse to God, and kept him strong against his tender compassion towards his son.
When the vngodly perished, she deliuered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell downe upon the fiue cities.

Of whose wickedness euen to this day the waste land that smoks, is a testimonie, and plants bearing fruite that never come to ripenesse: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an vnbeleeuing soul.

For regarding not wisdom, they gate not only this hurt, that they knew not the things which were good: but also left behind them to the world a memoriall of their foolishnes: so that in the things wherein they offended, they could not so much as be hid.
But Wisdom deliuered from paine those that attended upon her.

When the righteous fled from his brothers wrath, she guided him in right paths: showed him the kingdom of God: and gaue him knowledge of holy things, made him rich in his trauailes, and multiplied the fruit of his labours.
In the couetousnesse of such as oppressed him, she stood by him, and made him rich.
She defended him from his enemies, and kept him safe from those that lay in wait, and in a sore conflict she gaue him the victory, that he might knowe that godlinesse is stronger then all.
When the righteous was solde, she forsooke him not, but deliuered him from sin: she went downe with him into the pit,

And left him not in bonds till she brought him the scepter of the kingdom and power against those that oppressed him: as for them that had accused him, she showed them to be liers, and gaue them perpetuall glory.
She deliuered the righteous people, and blamelesse seed from the nation that oppressed them.
She entred into the soul of the seruant of the Lord, and withstood dreadfull kings in wonders and signes,
Rendred to the righteous a reward of their labours, guided them in a marueilous way, and was to them for a couer by day, and a light of starres in the night season:
Brought them through the red sea, and led them thorow much water.
But she drowned their enemies, and cast them up out of the bottome of the deepe.
Therefore the righteous spoiled the vngodly, & praised your holy Name, O Lord, and magnified with one accord your hand that fought for them.
For wisdom opened the mouth of the dumbe, and made the tongues of them that cannot speake, eloquent.

verses.t: She prospered their works in the hand of the holy Prophet.
They went thorough the wildernesse that was not inhabited, and pitched tents in places where there lay no way.
They stood against their enemies, and were auenged of their aduersaries.
When they were thirsty they called upon you, and water was given them out of the flinty rocke, and their thirst was quenched out of the hard stone.
For by what things their enemies were punished, by the same they in their neede were benefited.
For in stead of a fountaine of a perpetuall running riuer, troubled with foule blood,
For a manifest reproofe of that commandement, whereby the infants were slaine, you gau to them abundance of water by a meanes which they hoped not for,
Declaring by that thirst then, how you had punished their aduersaries.
For when they were tryed, albeit but in mercy chastised, they knew how the vngodly were judged in wrath and tormented thirsting in another maner then the Just.
For these you did admonish, and trie as a father: but the other as a seuere king you did condemne and punish.
Whether they were absent, or present, they were vexed alike.
For a double griefe came upon them, and a groaning for the remembrance of things past.
For when they heard by their own punishments the other to be benefited, they had some feeling of the Lord.
For whom they reiected with scorne when he was long before throwen out at the casting forth of the infants, him in the end, when they saw what came to passe, they admired.

But for the foolish deuises of their wickedness, wherewith being deceiued, they worshipped serpents voyd of reason, and vile beasts: you did send a multitude of vnreasonable beasts upon them for vengeance,
That they might knowe that wherewithall a man sins, by the same also shall he be punished.
For your Almighty hand that made the world of matter without forme, wanted not meanes to send among them a multitude of Beares, or fierce Lyons,
Or vnknowen wild beasts full of rage newly created, breathing out either a fiery vapour, or filthy sents of scattered smoake, or shooting horrible sparkles out of their eyes:
Whereof not onely the harme might dispatch them at once: but also the terrible sight vtterly destroy them.

Indeed and without these might they have fallen downe with one blast, being persecuted of vengeance, and scattered abroad thorough the breath of your power, but you have ordered all things in measure, and number, and weight.
For you can show your great strength at all times when you will, and who may withstand the power of your arme?
For the whole world before you is as a litle graine of the ballance, indeed as a drop of the morning dew that falls downe upon the earth.
But you have mercy upon all: for you can do all things, and wink at the sins of men: because they should amend.
For you lou all the things that are, and abhor nothing which you have made: for never would you have made any thing, if you had hated it.
And how could any thing have endured if it had not beene your will? or beene preserued, if not called by you?
But you spar all: for they are yours, O Lord, you louer of souls.

verses.t: For your vncorruptible spirit is in all things.
Therefore chastn you them by little, and little, that offend, and warn them by putting them in remembrance, wherin they have offended, that leauing their wickedness they may believe on you O Lord.
For it was your will to destroy by the handes of our fathers, both those old inhabitants of your holy land,
Whom you hatedst for doing most odious works of witchcrafts, and wicked sacrifices;
And also those mercilesse murderers of children, & deuourers of mans flesh, and the feasts of blood;
With their Priests out of the midst of their idolatrous crew, and the parents that killed with their own hands, souls destitute of helpe:
That the land which you esteemedst aboue all other, might receiue a worthy colonie of Gods children.
Neuerthelesse, euen those you sparedst as men, and did send waspes forerunners of your hoste, to destroy them by little and little.
Not that you were vnable to bring the vngodly under the hand of the righteous in battell, or to destroy them at once with cruel beastes, or with one rough word:

But executing your iudgements upon them by little and little, you gau them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughtie generation, and that their malice, was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.
For it was a cursed seed, from the beginning, neither did you for feare of any man give them pardon for those things wherein they sinned.

For who shall say, What have you done? or who shall withstand your judgment, or who shall accuse you for the nations that perish whom you have made? or who shall come to stand against you, to be reuenged for the unrighteous men?
For neither is there any God but you, that cares for all, to whom you might show that your judgment is not vnright.

For if you did punish the enemies of your children, and the condemned to death with such deliberation, giuing them time and place, wherby they might be deliuered from their malice.
With how great circumspection did you judge your own sons, to whose fathers you have sworne, and made couenants of good promises?

Therefore whereas you do chasten us, you scourg our enemies a thousand times more, to the intent that when we judge, we should carefully think of your goodnesse, and when we our selves are judged, we should looke for mercy.
Therefore, whereas men have lived dissolutely and vnrighteously, you have tormented them with their own abominations.

Therefore to them, as to children without the vse of reason, you did send a judgment to mocke them.

paragraphs: For your vncorruptible spirit is in all things. Therefore chastn you them by little, and little, that offend, and warn them by putting them in remembrance, wherin they have offended, that leauing their wickedness they may believe on you O Lord. For it was your will to destroy by the handes of our fathers, both those old inhabitants of your holy land, Whom you hatedst for doing most odious works of witchcrafts, and wicked sacrifices;

And also those mercilesse murderers of children, & deuourers of mans flesh, and the feasts of blood; With their Priests out of the midst of their idolatrous crew, and the parents that killed with their own hands, souls destitute of helpe: That the land which you esteemedst aboue all other, might receiue a worthy colonie of Gods children. Neuerthelesse, euen those you sparedst as men, and did send waspes forerunners of your hoste, to destroy them by little and little.

verses.t: Surely vaine are all men by nature, who are ignorant of God, and could not out of the good things that are seene, know him that is: neither by considering the works, did they acknowledge the work-master;
But deemed either fire, or wind, or the swift aire, or the circle of the stars, or the violent water, or the lights of heaven to be the gods which gouerne the world:
With whose beautie, if they being delighted, tooke them to be gods: let them know how much better the Lord of them is; for the first Author of beautie has created them.
But if they were astonished at their power and virtue, let them vnderstand by them, how much mightier he is that made them.
For by the greatnesse and beautie of the creatures, proportionably the Maker of them is seene.
But yet for this they are the lesse to be blamed: for they peraduenture erre seeking God, and desirous to find him.
For being conuersant in his works, they search him diligently, and believe their sight: because the things are beautifull that are seene.
However, neither are they to be pardoned.
For if they were able to know so much, that they could aime at the world; how did they not sooner find out the Lord of it?

But miserable are they, and in dead things is their hope, who called them gods which are the works of mens hands, golde and siluer, to shewe arte in, and resemblances of beasts, or a stone good for nothing, the work of an ancient hand.

Now a carpenter that fels timber, after he has sawen downe a tree meet for the purpose, and taken off all the barke skilfully round about, and has wrought it handsomely, & made a vessell of it fit for the seruice of mans life:
And after spending the refuse of his work to dresse his meat, has filled himself:

And taking the very refuse among those which serued to no vse (being a crooked piece of wood, and ful of knots) has carued it diligently when he had nothing else to do, and formed it by the skill of his vnderstanding, and fashioned it to the image of a man:
Or made it like some vile beast, laying it over with vermilion, and with paint, colouring it red, and couering every spot in it:
And when he had made a conuenient roume for it, set it in a wall, and made it fast with yron:
For he prouided for it, that it might not fall: knowing that it was vnable to helpe it self, (for it is an image and has neede of helpe:)
Then makes he prayer for his goods, for his wife and children, and is not ashamed to speake to that which has no life.

For health, he calls upon that which is weake: for life, prays to that which is dead: for aide, humbly beseeches that which has least meanes to helpe: and for a good iourney, he askes of that which cannot set a foot forward:
And for gaining and getting, and for good successe of his hands, askes abilitie to do, of him that is most vnable to do any thing.

verses.t: Again, one preparing himself to saile, and about to passe through the raging waues, calls upon a piece of wood more rotten then the vesell that caries him.
For verely desire of gaine deuised that, and the workeman built it by his skill:

For in the old time also when the proud gyants perished, the hope of the world gouerned by your hand, escaped in a weake vessell, and left to all ages a seed of generation.
For blessed is the wood, whereby righteousness comes.
But that which is made with hands, is cursed, aswell it, as he that made it: he, because he made it, and it, because being corruptible it was called God.
For the vngodly and his vngodlines are both alike hatefull to God.
For that which is made, shall be punished together with him that made it.

Therfore euen upon the idoles of the Gentiles shall there be a visitation: because in the creature of God they are become an abomination and stumbling blocks to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the vnwise.
For the deuising of idoles was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the inuention of them the corruption of life.
For neither were they from the beginning, neither shall they be for ever.
For by the vaine glory of men they entred into the world, and therefore shall they come shortly to an end.

For a father afflicted with vntimely mourning, when he has made an image of his childe soone taken away, now honoured him as a god, which was then a dead man, and deliuered to those that were under him, ceremonies and sacrifices.
Thus in processe of time an vngodly custome growen strong, was kept as a law, and grauen images were worshipped by the commandements of kings,

Whom men could not honor in presence, because they dwelt farre off, they tooke the counterfeit of his visage from farre, and made an expresse image of a king whom they honoured, to the end that by this their forwardnes, they might flatter him that was absent, as if he were present.
Also the singular diligence of the artificer did helpe to set forward the ignorant to more superstition.
For he peraduenture willing to please one in authority, forced all his skill to make the resemblance of the best fashion.
And so the multitude allured by the grace of the work, tooke him now for a god, which a litle before was but honoured as a man.
And this was an occasion to deceiue the world: for men seruing either calamitie or tyrannie, did ascribe to stones, and stockes, the incommunicable Name.
Moreouer this was not enough for them, that they erred in the knowledge of God, but whereas they lived in the great warre of ignorance, those so great plagues called they peace.
For whil they slew their children in sacrifices, or vsed secret ceremonies, or made reuellings of strange rites
They kept neither liues nor mariages any longer vndefiled: but either one slew another traiterously, or grieued him by adulterie:
So that there reigned in all men without exception, blood, manslaughter, theft, and dissimulation, corruption, vnfaithfulnesse, tumults, periurie,
Disquieting of good men, forgetfulnesse of good turnes, defiling of souls, changing of kinde, disorder in mariages, adulterie, and shameles vncleannesse.
For the worshipping of idoles not to be named, is the beginning, the cause, and the end of all evil.
For either they are mad when they be merry, or prophesie lies, or live vniustly, or else lightly forsweare themselues.
For insomuch as their trust is in idoles which have no life, though they sweare falsly, yet they looke not to be hurt.
However for both causes shal they be iustly punished: both because they thought not well of God, giuing heed to idols, and also vniustly swore in deceit, despising holinesse.
For it is not the power of them by whom they sweare: but it is the just vengeance of sinners, that punishes always the offence of the vngodly.

verses.t: But you O God, art gracious and true: long suffering, and in mercy ordering all things.
For if we sin we are yours, knowing your power: but we will not sin, knowing that we are counted yours.
For to know you is perfect righteousness: indeed to know your power is the roote of immortality.
For neither did the mischieuous inuention of men deceiue us: nor an image spotted with diuers colours, the painters fruitlesse labour.
The sight wherof entises fooles to lust after it, and so they desire the forme of a dead image that has no breath.
Both they that make them, they that desire them, and they that worship them, are louers of evil things, and are worthy to have such things to trust upon.

For the potter tempering soft earth fashions, every vessell with much labour for our seruice: indeed of the same clay he makes both the vessels that serue for clean vses: and likewise also all such as serue to the contrary: but what is the vse of either sort, the potter himself is the judge.

And employing his labours lewdly, he makes a vaine God of the same clay, euen he which a little before was made of earth himself, and within a little while after returns to the same out of the which he was taken: when his life which was lent him shall be demanded.

Notwithstanding his care is, not that he shall have much labour, nor that his life is short: but strius to excel goldsmiths, and siluersmiths, and endeuours to do like the workers in brasse, and counts it his glory to make counterfeit things.
His heart is ashes, his hope is more vile then earth, and his life of lesse value then clay:
Forasmuch as he knew not his maker, and him that inspired into him an actiue soul, and breathed in a living spirit.
But they counted our life a pastime, & our time here a market for gaine: for, say they, we must be getting every way, though it be by evil meanes.
For this man that of earthly matter makes brickle vessels, and grauen images, knows himself to offend aboue all others.
And all the enemies of your people, that hold them in subiection are most foolish and are more miserable then very babes.

For they counted all the idoles of the heathen to be gods: which neither have the vse of eyes to see, nor noses to draw breath, nor eares to heare, nor fingers of hands to handle, and as for their feete they are slow to go.
For man made them, and he that borrowed his own spirit fashioned them, but no man can make a god like to himself.
For being mortall he works a dead thing with wicked hands: for he himself is better then the things which he worships: whereas he lived once, but they never.
Indeed they worshipped those beasts also that are most hatefull: for being compared together, some are worse then others.

verses.t: Therefore by the like were they punished worthily, and by the multitude of beasts tormented.
In stead of which punishment, dealing graciously with your own people you preparedst for them meate of a strange taste: euen quailes to stirre up their appetite:

To the end that they desiring food might for the ougly sight of the beasts sent among them, loath euen that which they must needs desire: but these suffering penury for a short space, might be made partakers of a strange taste.
For it was requisite, that upon them excercising tyranny should come penury which they could not auoyde: but to these it should onely be showed how their enemies were tormented.
For when the horrible fiercenesse of beasts came upon these, and they perished with the stings of crooked serpents, your wrath endured not for ever.
But they were troubled for a smal season that they might be admonished, hauing a signe of saluation, to put them in remembrance of the commandement of your Law.
For he that turned himself towards it, was not saved by the thing that he saw: but by you that art the savior of all.
And in this you made your enemies confesse, that it is you who deliuer from all evil:
For them the bitings of grassehoppers and flies killed, neither was there found any remedy for their life: for they were worthy to be punished by such.
But your sons, not the very teeth of venemous dragons ouercame: for your mercy was ever by them, and healed them.
For they were pricked, that they should remember your words, and were quickly saved, that not falling into deep forgetfulnesse, they might be continually mindefull of your goodnesse.
For it was neither herbe, nor mollifying plaister that restored them to health: but your word, O Lord, which heals all things.
For you have power of life and death: you lead to the gates of hell, and bring up again.
A man indeed kills through his malice: and the spirit when it is gone foorth returns not; neither the soul receiued up, comes again.
But it is not possible to escape your hand.

For the vngodly that denied to know you, were scourged by the strength of your arme: with strange raines, hailes, and showers were they persecuted, that they could not auoyd, and through fire were they consumed.
For, which is most to be wondered at, the fire had more force in the water that quenches all things: for the world fights for the righteous.

For sometimes the flame was mitigated, that it might not burne up the beasts that were sent against the vngodly: but themselues might see and perceiue that they were persecuted with the judgment of God.
And at another time it burns euen in the midst of water, aboue the power of fire, that it might destroy the fruits of an vniust land.
In stead whereof you fed your own people, with Angels food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every mans delight, and agreeing to every taste.
For your sustenance declared your sweetnesse to your children, and seruing to the appetite of the eater tempered it self to every mans liking.
But snow and yce endured the fire and melted not, that they might know that fire burning the haile, and sparkling in the raine, did destroy the fruits of the enemies.
But this again did euen forget his own strength, that the righteous might be nourished.
For the creature that serus you who art the maker, encreases his strength against the unrighteous for their punishment, and abats his strength for the benefit of such as put their trust in you.
Therefore euen then was it altered into all fashions, and was obedient to your grace that nourishes all things, according to the desire of them that had need:
That your children, O Lord, whom you lou, might know that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word which preserus them that put their trust in you.
For that which was not destroied of the fire, being warmed with a litle Sun beame, soone melted away,
That it might be knowen, that we must preuent the Sun, to give you thanks, and at the day-spring pray to you.
For the hope of the vnfaithfull, shal melt away as the Winters hoarefrost, and shall runne away as vnprofitable water.

And in this you made your enemies confesse, that it is you who deliuer from all evil: For them the bitings of grassehoppers and flies killed, neither was there found any remedy for their life: for they were worthy to be punished by such. But your sons, not the very teeth of venemous dragons ouercame: for your mercy was ever by them, and healed them.

For they were pricked, that they should remember your words, and were quickly saved, that not falling into deep forgetfulnesse, they might be continually mindefull of your goodnesse. For it was neither herbe, nor mollifying plaister that restored them to health: but your word, O Lord, which heals all things. For you have power of life and death: you lead to the gates of hell, and bring up again. A man indeed kills through his malice: and the spirit when it is gone foorth returns not; neither the soul receiued up, comes again.

But it is not possible to escape your hand. For the vngodly that denied to know you, were scourged by the strength of your arme: with strange raines, hailes, and showers were they persecuted, that they could not auoyd, and through fire were they consumed. For, which is most to be wondered at, the fire had more force in the water that quenches all things: for the world fights for the righteous. For sometimes the flame was mitigated, that it might not burne up the beasts that were sent against the vngodly: but themselues might see and perceiue that they were persecuted with the judgment of God.

And at another time it burns euen in the midst of water, aboue the power of fire, that it might destroy the fruits of an vniust land. In stead whereof you fed your own people, with Angels food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every mans delight, and agreeing to every taste. For your sustenance declared your sweetnesse to your children, and seruing to the appetite of the eater tempered it self to every mans liking.

But snow and yce endured the fire and melted not, that they might know that fire burning the haile, and sparkling in the raine, did destroy the fruits of the enemies. But this again did euen forget his own strength, that the righteous might be nourished. For the creature that serus you who art the maker, encreases his strength against the unrighteous for their punishment, and abats his strength for the benefit of such as put their trust in you.

Therefore euen then was it altered into all fashions, and was obedient to your grace that nourishes all things, according to the desire of them that had need: That your children, O Lord, whom you lou, might know that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word which preserus them that put their trust in you. For that which was not destroied of the fire, being warmed with a litle Sun beame, soone melted away,

That it might be knowen, that we must preuent the Sun, to give you thanks, and at the day-spring pray to you. For the hope of the vnfaithfull, shal melt away as the Winters hoarefrost, and shall runne away as vnprofitable water.

verses.t: For great are your Iudgements, and cannot be expressed: therefore vnnourtured souls have erred.

For when unrighteous men thought to oppresse the holy nation: they being shut up in their houses, the prisoners of darkness, and fettered with the bondes of a long night, lay exiled from the eternall prouidence.
For while they supposed to lie hid in their secret sins, they were scattered under a darke vaile of forgetfulnesse, being horribly astonished, and troubled with (strange) apparitions.
For neither might the corner that helde them keepe them from feare: but noises (as of waters) falling downe, sounded about them, and sadde visions appeared to them with heavy countenances.
No power of the fire might give them light: neither could the bright flames of the starres endure to lighten that horrible night.
Onely there appeared to them a fire kindled of it self, very dreadfull: for being much terrified, they thought the things which they saw to be worse then the sight they saw not.
As for the illusions of arte Magicke, they were put downe, and their vaunting in wisdom was reprooued with disgrace.
For they that promised to driue away terrours, and troubles from a sicke soul, were sicke themselues of feare worthy to be laughed at.
For though no terrible thing did feare them: yet being skared with beasts that passed by, and hissing of serpents,
They died for feare, denying that they saw the ayre, which could of no side be auoided.
For wickedness condemned by her own witness, is very timorous, and being pressed with conscience, always forecasts grieuous things.
For feare is nothing else, but a betraying of the succours which reason offers.
And the expectation from within being lesse, counts the ignorance more then the cause which brings the torment.
But they sleeping the same sleepe that night which was indeed intolerable, and which came upon them out of the bottomes of ineuitable hell:
Were partly vexed with monstrous apparitions, and partly fainted, their heart failing them: for a suddaine feare and not looked for, came upon them.
So then, whosoeuer there fell downe, was straitly kept, shut up in a prison without yron barres.
For whether he were farmer, or shepherd, or a labourer in the field, he was ouertaken, and endured that necessitie, which could not be auoided: for they were all bound with one chaine of darkness.
Whether it were a whistling winde, or a melodious noise of birdes among the spreading branches, or a pleasing fall of water running violently:

Or a terrible sound of stones cast downe, or a running that could not be seene of skipping beasts, or a roaring voice of most sauage wilde beasts, or a rebounding Eccho from the hollow mountaines: these things made them to swoone for feare.
For the whole world shined with cleare light, and none were hindered in their labour.
Over them onely was spread an heavy night, an image of that darkness which should afterwards receiue them: but yet were they to themselues more grieuous then the darkness.

verses.t: Neuerthelesse, your Saints had a very great light, whose voice they hearing and not seeing their shape, because they also had not suffered the same things, they counted them happy.
But for that they did not hurt them now, of whom they had beene wronged before, they thanked them, and besought them pardon, for that they had beene enemies.
In stead whereof you gau them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the vnknowen iourney, and an harmelesse Sun to entertaine them honourably.
For they were worthy to be depriued of light, and imprisoned in darknesse, who had kept your sons shut up, by whom the vncorrupt light of the law was to be given to the world.

And when they had determined to slay the babes of the Saints, one child being cast forth, and saved: to reproue them, you took away the multitude of their children, and destroyedst them altogether in a mightie water.
Of that night were our fathers certified afore, that assuredly knowing to what oathes they had given credence, they might afterwards be of good cheere.
So of your people was accepted both the saluation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.
For wherewith you did punish our aduersaries, by the same you did glorifie us whom you had called.

For the righteous children of good men did sacrifice secretly, and with one consent made a holy lawe, that the Saints should be alike partakers of the same good and evil, the fathers now singing out the songs of praise.
But on the other side there sounded an ill-according crie of the enemies, and a lamentable noise was caried abroad for children that were bewailed.
The master and the seruaunt were punished after one maner, and like as the king, so suffered the common person.
So they altogether had innumerable dead with one kind of death, neither were the living sufficient to burie them: for in one moment the nobl ofspring of them was destroyed.
For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments, upon the destruction of the first borne, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.
For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course,
Your almighty word leapt downe from heaven, out of your royall throne, as a fierce man of warre into the midst of a land of destruction,
And brought your vnfained commandement as a sharpe sword, and standing up filled all things with death, and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.
Then suddenly visions of horrible dreames troubled them sore, and terrours came upon them vnlooked for.
And one throwen here, another there halfe dead, showed the cause of his death.
For the dreames that troubled them, did foreshew this, lest they should perish, and not know why they were afflicted.
Indeed, the tasting of death touched the righteous also, and there was a destruction of the multitude in the wildernes: but the wrath endured not long.

For then the blamelesse man made haste, and stood foorth to defend them, and bringing the shield of his proper ministerie, euen prayer and the propitiation of incense, set himself against the wrath, and so brought the calamity to an end, declaring that he was your seruant.
So he ouercame the destroyer, not with strength of body, nor force of armes, but with a word subdued he him that punished, alleaging the oathes and couenants made with the fathers.
For when the dead were now fallen downe by heaps one upon another, standing betweene, he staied the wrath, and parted the way to the living.
For in the long garment was the whole world, & in the foure rowes of the stones was the glory of the fathers grauen, and your maiestie upon the diademe of his head.
To these the destroyer gaue place, and was afraid of them: for it was enough that they onely tasted of the wrath.

verses.t: As for the vngodly, wrath came upon them without mercy to the end: for he knew before what they would do;
Howe that hauing given them leaue to depart, and sent them hastily away, they would repent and pursue them.
For whil they were yet mourning, and making lamentation at the graues of the dead, they added another foolish deuice, and pursued them as fugitiues, whom they had entreated to be gone.

For the destiny, whereof they were worthy, drew them to this end, and made them forget the things that had already happened, that they might fulfill the punishment which was wanting to their torments,
And that your people might passe a wonderfull way: but they might find a strange death.
For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, seruing the peculiar commandements that were given to them, that your children might be kept without hurt.
As namely, a cloud shadowing the campe, and where water stood before drie land appeared, and out of the red Sea a way without impediment, and out of the violent streame a greene field:
Where-thorough all the people went that were defended with your hand, seeing your marueilous strange wonders.
For they went at large like horses, and leaped like lambes, praising you O Lord, who had deliuered them.

For they were yet mindefull of the things that were done while they soiourned in the strange land, how the ground brought forth flies in stead of cattell, and how the riuer cast up a multitude of frogs in stead of fishes.
But afterwards they saw a new generation of foules, when being led with their appetite they asked delicate meates.
For quailes came up to them from the Sea, for their contentment.

And punishments came upon the sinners not without former signes by the force of thunders: for they suffered iustly, according to their own wickedness, insomuch as they vsed a more hard and hatefull behauiour towards strangers:
For the Sodomits did not receiue those whom they knew not when they came: but these brought friends into bondage, that had well deserued of them.
And not onely so: but peraduenture some respect shall be had of those, because they vsed strangers not friendly.
But these very grieuously afflicted them, whom they had receiued with feastings, and were already made partakers of the same lawes with them.

Therefore euen with blindnesse were these stricken, as those were at the doores of the righteous man: when being compassed about with horrible great darknesse, every one sought the passage of his own doores.

For the elements were changed in themselues by a kind of harmonie, like as in a Psaltery notes change the name of the tune, and yet are always sounds, which may well be perceiued by the sight of the things that have beene done.
For earthly things were turned into watry, and the things that before swamme in the water, now went upon the ground.
The fire had power in the water, forgetting his own virtue: and the water forgat his own quenching nature.
On the other side, the flames wasted not the flesh of the corruptible living things, though they walked therin, neither melted they the ycie kind of heavenly meate, that was of nature apt to melt.
For in all things, O Lord, you did magnifie your people, and glorifie them, neither did you lightly regard them: but did assist them in every time and place.
